doc.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011

title: Learning guitar in hospital from teacher George Dell
summary: Hip problem kept him in hospital for three years; a ukulele led to lessons from former CBS guitarist George Dell, and parents were glad.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Okay. I heard, because I’m not from this area, I didn’t quite know you a real long time ago. I heard something about George Dell, the music store owner, visiting you when you were laid up or something, to give you a start. Is that true?

Oh yeah, yeah. What happened, as a child I had a problem with my hip. And so I was in the hospital for an extended period of time while they were finding different surgeries and therapies to try to get me to be able to walk. As a result I was in the hospital for more than three years, without going home. And this happened at the time I was between nine and eleven or something like that. So to try to give me something to do, one of my aunts brought me a little plastic ukulele and I’m sitting there figuring stuff out on it. And I said hey this is pretty cool. I’ve got an old guitar in the attic, let me dig that out. And so they brought me this old horrible guitar. And by myself I was just messing around, it was a toy to me, I was figuring stuff out. So it got noticed by the people in the hospital and they said well we need a teacher to come in to give this kid something to do so he stops terrorizing the nurses. So the bottom line is the guy that came over to teach me was originally a studio guitarist, I believe for CBS in New York, his name was George O’Dell, he called himself George Dell, and he had a band called the Dell Trio. Well when © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

he retired from professional music in New York, he came back to his wife’s home town which was Utica, and the wife used to be a nurse at what is now Faxton Hospital, then it was Children’s Hospital. So they called her and said hey, your husband teaches? You want to send him up and teach this kid we got? And so he would come up and give me a half hour lesson. However, his wife would be in the nurse’s lounge having coffee, talking to her old cronies, and the half hour lesson would become 45 minutes, an hour, an hour and a half. So as long as she kept chatting he kept giving me longer and longer lessons. It was great for me I had nothing else to do. So I had this really good conscientious teacher that loved to talk, and I was as fond of eating it up. So that’s how I got my start.
Were your parents happy to see this going on?
Were your parents happy to see this going on?
Oh absolutely. Anything from keeping me from being a crazy kid.
Yeah. Well it must have been hard. Did you have tutors coming in too?
At that time they actually had a school room, so they had a one room schoolhouse kind of situation so I still kept up my studies.
